text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Lithuanian foreign minister Algirdas Saudargas arrives today on his first official visit to Latvia.

- An interview with Dimitris Demekas, permanent representative of the IMF in Latvia. He said that Latvia's fiscal and monetary policies were on track and predicted that the country's GDP will grow by four percent this year.
- The process of preparing a U.S.-Baltic charter will be accelerated in the wake of the NATO-Russia agreement, White House officials said on Friday.
- It was decided in Moscow that the first meeting of the joint Russian-Latvian intergovernmental commission will take place between June 9-20.
- The Italian president, Oscar Luiggi Scalfaro, will arrive on his first official visit tyo Latvia later this week.

- The district court of Riga will resume consideration of a 50-million lat suit brought by the Latvian Shipping Company against the national electricity producer, Latvenergo. The debt dates back to 1992, when the Russian government decided to settle its $37.5 million debt to the Latvian Shipping Company with natural gas supplies.
- The second Expo Latvia exhibition will be held in Novgorod, Russia, displaying 36 Latvian companies.
- Last year Latvia was the largest exporter of round timber and firewood to Sweden.
